draft.title: Acute responses in Unit 3
card: Acute responses are the immediate changes the body makes during a single session of exercise. They happen together to supply energy to working muscles.
Cardiovascular
heart rate and stroke volume rise, so cardiac output rises. More blood is sent to the working muscles.
Respiratory
breathing rate and the depth of each breath rise, so more air moves in and out of the lungs. This brings in more oxygen and removes carbon dioxide.
Muscular
working muscles take up more oxygen from the blood, and more motor units are recruited to produce force.
draft.remember: One session of exercise triggers linked changes in heart, lungs and muscles.

a.q: Which change is an acute cardiovascular response to exercise?
opts: Cardiac output rises to send more blood to muscles
Breathing rate rises to bring in more air
Muscles take up more oxygen from the blood
Muscles grow larger after weeks of training
a.why: A rise in cardiac output is a cardiovascular change during a session. A faster breathing rate is respiratory, and muscle growth over weeks is a long-term change, not an acute one.
a.clue: Think about the heart and blood vessels only.

b.q: Tom starts a hard rowing session. Which response helps get oxygen from the lungs into his bloodstream?
opts: Deeper and faster breathing
A rise in stroke volume
More motor units recruited
A rise in heart rate
b.why: Deeper and faster breaths move more air through the lungs, which is a respiratory response. Heart rate and stroke volume move blood around, and motor units are a muscular response.
b.clue: Which system moves air in and out?

a.best: Cardiac output rises to send more blood to muscles

problems.detail: The stem asks what gets oxygen 'from the lungs into his bloodstream'. That is gas exchange (pulmonary diffusion), not moving air into the lungs. Higher heart rate and stroke volume raise blood flow through the lung capillaries, which increases oxygen uptake into the blood, so a careful teacher could defend those options too. Reword to ask which response moves more air in and out of the lungs.
The clue 'Which system moves air in and out?' does not match the stem, which is about oxygen entering the blood. It also points straight to the intended answer instead of helping the student think.

The why says heart rate and stroke volume only 'move blood around'. A rise in cardiac output also increases pulmonary blood flow and so helps oxygen diffuse from the lungs into the blood. This teaches a misleading split between the systems.

The heart rate and stroke volume options are also defensible, and the clue and why reinforce the confusion. Reword b to ask about moving air in and out of the lungs.
